## Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of soil color under
controlled laboratory lighting using the Munsell Soil Color Charts.
Soil color is a rapid, non-destructive indicator of organic matter
content, mineralogy, drainage condition, and degree of weathering. It
is a required observation in soil profile descriptions and is used in
soil taxonomy (e.g., distinguishing Mollisols by dark surface colors)
[@soilsurveystaff2017; @lynn2009].

Field color determinations (see
[SOP-F400](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)) are affected by
variable natural lighting, sun angle, and observer fatigue. This
laboratory procedure standardizes the observation under a controlled
illuminant to improve reproducibility and provide a reference-quality
color record.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All soil and sediment samples for which a
  reference-quality Munsell color determination is needed, including
  both moist and air-dried conditions
- **Does not apply to:** Rock or mineral color determinations using the
  Munsell Rock Color Chart, instrumental colorimetry or
  spectrophotometry, or quick field assessments (which remain valuable
  but are less reproducible)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Perform color determinations, record results |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |

## Definitions

- **Chroma:** The colorimetric purity or saturation of a color; the third component of Munsell notation (e.g., the 4 in 10YR 4/4); higher chroma values indicate more saturated, vivid colors; low chroma (less than or equal to 2) in subsurface horizons indicates gleying and periodic saturation.
- **Hue:** The dominant spectral color in Munsell notation (e.g., 10YR, 7.5YR, 2.5Y, Gley 1); corresponds to the wavelength of the dominant reflected light; the first element of a Munsell color designation.
- **Munsell color system:** A standardized color notation developed by A.H. Munsell expressing color as three independent components: Hue, Value, and Chroma; used universally in soil science for objective color description.
- **Redoximorphic features:** Color patterns in soil caused by reduction and oxidation of iron and manganese under fluctuating saturation conditions; include masses (concentrations), depletions (zones of low chroma), and concretions; diagnostic for hydric soils.
- **Standard illuminant (D65):** A standardized daylight spectrum at 6,500 K color temperature; the reference lighting condition for accurate Munsell color matching; overcast north-sky light or a D65 light box approximates this condition.
- **Value:** The lightness or darkness of a color in Munsell notation; ranges from 0 (black) to 10 (white); the second component in Munsell notation (e.g., the 4 in 10YR 4/4).


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Soil samples may contain pathogens. Wash hands after
  handling soil.
- **Physical:** No significant hazards. If using a spray bottle to
  moisten samples, avoid wetting electronic equipment or Munsell
  charts.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Lab coat


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Munsell Soil Color Charts (current edition) | Replace when pages are faded, stained, or damaged |
| Daylight-balanced lamp (D65 or equivalent, 5,000--6,500 K) | Position to illuminate the sample and chart evenly without glare |
| Spray bottle with deionized water     | For moistening air-dried samples |
| White ceramic tile or neutral gray card | For calibrating eye to neutral |
| Spatula or palette knife              | For preparing a smooth sample surface |
| Lab notebook or standardized data sheet | For recording results       |


## Procedure

### Lighting Setup

1. Position the daylight-balanced lamp so it illuminates the sample and
   the Munsell chart at approximately the same angle and distance
2. Avoid mixing light sources (turn off overhead fluorescent or LED
   room lights if their color temperature differs significantly from
   the reference lamp)
3. Allow the lamp to warm up for at least 5 minutes before beginning
   observations

::: {.callout-note}
If a daylight-balanced lamp is not available, work near a north-facing
window under overcast sky conditions. Avoid direct sunlight, which
changes color temperature with sun angle and clouds.
:::

### Sample Preparation

1. For **moist** color: if the sample is already field-moist, proceed
   directly. If it has been air-dried, moisten a subsample by adding
   deionized water drop by drop with a spray bottle or pipette until
   the sample glistens but no free water pools on the surface
   [@soilsurveystaff2017]
2. For **dry** color: use the air-dried sample without adding water
3. Use a spatula to press the soil into a smooth, flat surface
   (approximately 2--3 cm diameter) on a white or neutral background.
   A rough surface creates shadows that bias the reading toward darker
   values.
4. If the sample is heterogeneous (e.g., redoximorphic features),
   determine the color of the matrix and the color of each distinct
   mottle or concentration separately

### Color Determination

1. Hold the Munsell chart adjacent to the prepared sample so both are
   under the same illumination
2. Look through the apertures on the chart page, placing the sample
   behind each hole, to find the closest match
3. First identify the correct **hue** page (e.g., 10YR, 7.5YR, 2.5Y)
4. Then match the **value** (lightness, vertical axis) and **chroma**
   (saturation, horizontal axis) within that page
5. Record the Munsell notation in the format: hue value/chroma (e.g.,
   10YR 4/3)
6. If the sample falls between two chips, record the interpolated
   notation or the nearest chip with a note (e.g., "10YR 4/3 to 4/4")
7. Repeat the determination for both moist and dry conditions

::: {.callout-tip}
Color vision varies between individuals and can shift with fatigue.
For critical determinations, have two observers independently determine
the color and compare results. If readings differ by more than one
chip in any dimension, re-examine jointly.
:::

### Recording Results

Record the following for each sample:

- Sample ID and depth
- Munsell notation (moist)
- Munsell notation (dry)
- Descriptive color name from the chart (e.g., "dark yellowish brown")
- Any redoximorphic features (mottle color, abundance, size, contrast)
- Observer name(s)
- Date and lighting conditions

### Special Cases

**Redoximorphic features:** When mottles or concentrations are present,
record the matrix color and the color, abundance (few, common, many),
size (fine, medium, coarse), and contrast (faint, distinct, prominent)
of each type of feature per the standards in the Soil Survey Manual
[@soilsurveystaff2017].

**Very dark samples (value 2 or less):** These may be difficult to
distinguish on the chart. Prepare a thinner smear and confirm under
slightly brighter illumination.

**Effervescent or calcareous samples:** Note the presence of
carbonates (tested with dilute HCl per
[SOP-L402](SOP-L402-soil-pH-salinity.qmd)), as carbonate coatings
affect apparent color.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Perform duplicate readings (by the same or a second observer) on at
  least 10% of samples
- Acceptable agreement: readings should match within one chip in value
  and one chip in chroma on the same hue page
- Inspect the Munsell chart for fading or staining at the start of each
  session; replace if the neutral chip (N/) no longer appears true gray
- Record the lamp model and approximate color temperature in the lab
  notebook


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used soil subsamples          | Return to sample container or standard trash |
| No chemical waste generated   | --                                       |

## Training Record

Before performing Munsell color determinations independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Review the introductory pages of the Munsell Soil Color Charts
3. Practice matching at least 10 samples under supervision and compare
   readings with a trained observer
4. Demonstrate agreement within one chip in value and chroma on
   duplicate determinations
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
